clue.text: To leave university is a real disappointment

definitions.meaning: students go down from Oxford or Cambridge when they leave
a humiliating fall in status or a let-down

explanation.surface: A graduate finds that quitting college is a big let-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming down is the British term for leaving university, and a comedown is a deflating drop in fortune.

clue.text: Book subscription too often renewed

indicators.note: renewed means made over afresh, so these letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A book club membership keeps renewing itself far too frequently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renewed' shuffles TOO OFTEN. 'Subscription' is used in its old sense of something written underneath, here at the foot of a page.
explanation.definitionFit: A note printed at the bottom of a page in a book is literally a writing beneath the text.

clue.text: Could be maintained that only one of the cricket team is unfit

definitions.meaning: able to be held or defended

definitions.text: only one of the cricket team is unfit
definitions.meaning: a cricket side has eleven players, so with one injured, ten are able

explanation.surface: A captain argues that his claim of just one injured player holds up.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as TEN ABLE: eleven in a cricket team, one unfit, ten fit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenable position is one that can be defended or held.

clue.text: Let's put up the French girl

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as the letters of the word, without its apostrophe
la is the French feminine word for the

explanation.surface: Someone suggests giving a French girl a place to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'put up' as giving someone lodging; in a down clue it turns the word upward, and the apostrophe in 'Let's' is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Stella is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Greycoat general means to find room for manoeuvre

parts.note: Robert E. Lee led the grey-uniformed Confederate army in the American Civil War
a way is a means or method

explanation.surface: A Confederate commander looks for a method to gain space to manoeuvre.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is freedom or margin to act as one wishes.

clue.text: Grin widely to display anger

definitions.meaning: smile broadly enough for the teeth to show
bare the teeth in a snarl as a threat

explanation.surface: A broad smile can also be a sign of fury.
explanation.definitionFit: Baring teeth fits both a wide smile and an animal's snarl of hostility.

clue.text: Secretly follow case representing opposition to government

parts.note: to shadow someone is to trail them covertly
a cabinet is a case or cupboard for storage

explanation.surface: A spy trails a briefcase thought to hold anti-government papers.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the main opposition party names spokespeople mirroring each minister, forming an alternative ministerial team.

clue.text: The early hand a model described as very fit

indicators.note: to model is to shape or mould, so these letters are formed into something new

explanation.surface: A morning farmhand and a fashion model are both said to be in great shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' rearranges THE EARLY HAND A; 'described as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means vigorous and in robust health, especially in old age.

clue.text: Arrive just in time to succeed as a manufacturer

definitions.meaning: get there with seconds to spare
a maker produces things, read literally as producing it

explanation.surface: A factory owner's tale of punctuality and commercial triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom covers getting somewhere in time, achieving success, and literally producing an item.

clue.text: Nothing is wrong if everyone is dressed like a dandy

parts.note: all means every person
swell is an old adjective for smartly or fashionably dressed

explanation.surface: Everything is fine provided the whole company turns out looking elegant.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'is' as part of the answer's own phrase, but SWELL supplies the S; 'is' and 'if' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a reassurance that things are in good order.

clue.text: Return of prohibition leads to arrest

indicators.note: return means going back, so the word for prohibition is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition

explanation.surface: The reintroduction of a ban results in people being detained.
explanation.definitionFit: To nab someone is informal for to catch and detain them.

clue.text: Florid style of two colonels after other ranks retreat

indicators.note: after places the colonels following the retreating ranks
to retreat is to go backwards, so the abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, the non-officers
Col is the abbreviation for colonel, here given as CO each time
the second of the pair

explanation.surface: A pair of senior officers advance while ordinary soldiers fall back.
explanation.definitionFit: Rococo is an ornate eighteenth-century decorative manner full of elaborate flourishes.

clue.text: When women propose disposing of an early ape

indicators.note: disposing in the sense of arranging, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Getting rid of a primitive primate, oddly linked to marriage proposals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposing of' arranges EARLY APE; 'an' is a link. Tradition lets women propose on 29 February.
explanation.definitionFit: Folk custom holds that a woman may ask a man to marry her in the year with an extra February day.

clue.text: Drink up chum

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: to lap is to drink with the tongue, as a cat does

explanation.surface: An invitation to a friend to finish their glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Pal and chum are both informal words for a friend.

clue.text: Descent retraced from sweet Otto perhaps

indicators.note: retraced suggests tracing the letters again in another sequence

explanation.surface: Tracing a family's ancestry back from a fragrant forebear named Otto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retraced' rearranges DESCENT. Otto, or attar, is a perfume oil from roses, so 'Otto' looks like a name but is the fragrance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something perfumed with attar of roses is fragrant.

clue.text: Rubbish tip up the hill

indicators.note: in a down clue, tip up means the word is turned over from bottom to top

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: Dumped waste piles up into a mound.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'rubbish tip' is a British dump; here 'tip up' is the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tor is a rocky peak, especially on Dartmoor.

clue.text: Oddly enough they are also called downs

definitions.text: Oddly enough they are also called downs

parts.words: Oddly enough they are also called downs
parts.note: high open grassy country is curiously known as downs, though the land rises

explanation.surface: A wry observation on the contradictory naming of hilly country.
explanation.definitionFit: Downs are rolling chalk hills, that is, raised terrain.

clue.text: All round genius from tech taking maths endlessly

parts.note: a tech or poly is a British polytechnic college

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: A brilliant all-rounder emerges from a technical college that has been doing sums forever.
explanation.definitionFit: A polymath is a person learned across many fields.

clue.text: It runs up a Sicilian volcano with a long stride

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the volcano's name is read bottom to top

parts.note: Etna is the active volcano on Sicily
a lope is a long, easy bounding stride

explanation.surface: Something bounds up the slopes of Etna in great strides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link; the definition is just 'It runs'.
explanation.definitionFit: This hoofed African grazer is famed as a swift runner.

clue.text: Nuts lie scattered in the kitchen drawer possibly

indicators.note: scattered means strewn about, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Spilled nuts end up lying in the kitchen drawer.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen implement such as a spatula is found in a drawer, so the definition is by example.

clue.text: Recondite summary

definitions.meaning: obscure and hard to understand, theoretical
a short précis of a paper

explanation.surface: An obscure digest.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstract means both theoretical or abstruse and a brief résumé of an article.

clue.text: Everything French journalist sought to sell

parts.note: tout is French for all or everything
ed is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A French reporter tried to sell absolutely everything.
explanation.definitionFit: To tout goods is to solicit buyers pushily, so touted is past-tense peddled.

clue.text: Tips for making a ground spice

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Advice on how to make powdered seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' rearranges A and SPICE, with the indicator sitting between them; 'for making' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Apices is the plural of apex, a peak or point.

clue.text: Refuse what the walking wounded managed to do without

definitions.text: what the walking wounded managed to do without
definitions.meaning: a stretcher for carrying casualties, unneeded by those who can walk

explanation.surface: Lightly injured soldiers are spared the stretcher and the rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Litter is both waste dropped about and a stretcher for carrying the injured.

clue.text: Part of chapel yet to be declared a cathedral

indicators.note: part of says the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A chapel section has yet to be granted cathedral status.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be declared a' links to the definition, Ely in Cambridgeshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Ely Cathedral is a famous English church, so the city name stands for it.

clue.text: Where nuclear physicists hope to find power solution

definitions.text: Where nuclear physicists hope to find power
definitions.meaning: read as two words, inside nuclear fusion, the hoped-for energy source
a liquid made by steeping, such as tea

explanation.surface: Physicists seek energy in fusion and a liquid answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An infusion is a liquid in which herbs are steeped; split, it says inside the merging of nuclei.

clue.text: How one in 1050 or 500 addressed an English gent abroad

indicators.note: in places the single letter inside the Roman figure

parts.note: in Roman numerals M is 1000 and L is 50
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A Roman-numeral puzzle about greeting a gentleman travelling overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How' is a link opening the definition; the answer is what Continentals called an English nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Milord was the Continental form of address for an English lord or gentleman.

clue.text: There will be trouble if it is Old Nick's turn to shout

definitions.meaning: an idiom warning of serious consequences
Old Nick is Satan, and a shout is a British turn to buy drinks

explanation.surface: Trouble looms when Satan's round comes up at the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means grave consequences; literally it is Satan who must pay.
